history.summary: FLAG: NON-HINDU RECORD - Bathouism is the indigenous religion of the Bodo people, not Hinduism; keep-or-drop decision needed. The Karuwabasti Bodo Bathou Mandir is a Bathou Thansali (sacred worship space) established by the Bodo community at Karuwabasti Sivapur (Ward No. 9), Itanagar. Worship centres on Bathou Bwrai, the formless supreme god, represented by the living Sijou tree (Euphorbia splendens) - Bathouism traditionally prohibits idol worship. 'Bathou' combines 'Ba' (five) and 'thou' (deep), referring to the five elements (earth, water, air, fire, sky). Kherai is the major ritual festival, led by a priest (Oja) and the trance-dancing Doudini. No published founding date. COORDINATES ARE APPROXIMATE: city-level Itanagar point used (verify).

town_description: Itanagar, the capital of Arunachal Pradesh in Papum Pare district, sits in the Himalayan foothills. Named after the 14th-15th century Ita Fort, it is the state's administrative and cultural centre - home to the Jawaharlal Nehru State Museum, Ganga Lake and several Buddhist gompas, with a mix of tribal (Nyishi) and migrant communities.
